title: Tunable annealing of defects in self-aligning active crystals
abstract: Obtaining defect-free single-crystals is of crucial importance in soft matter and materials science, spanning both fundamental interests and practical applications. Active crystals, encompassing diverse dense systems from living organisms to artificial metamaterials, can offer a promising platform for autonomous structural reorganization. We demonstrate that increasing spatiotemporal orientational fluctuations around the mean polarized state can enhance crystallographic order in active crystals. Poly-to-single-crystal transformations in defect-rich, self-aligned active Brownian crystals with coupled translational-rotational dynamics are investigated. We show that long-lived persistence with slow alignment controls the defect-annealing capability. By disentangling activity magnitude from associated timescales, we reveal activity-assisted annealing. Tuning the persistence length enables overcoming thermal energy barriers. Simultaneously adjusting persistence and alignment timescales can tune relaxation from `fast' to `slow', yielding defect-rich and defect-free crystals, respectively. Furthermore, active crystals of point particles are found to exhibit similar defect annealing when flocking is delayed by tuning the timescale of the velocity relaxation towards the polarized state. These findings suggest that the mechanism may extend to a broader class of active crystals. Our results intersect statistical physics of living soft matter with the mechanics of defects and microstructures, proposing a nonequilibrium route towards reconfigurable materials.
summary: This work explores how active matter systems, modeled as active crystals, can self-heal defects to achieve perfect single-crystal order. By controlling the timescales associated with particle persistence and alignment, researchers demonstrated a tunable, activity-assisted annealing mechanism. This provides a non-equilibrium route for designing reconfigurable soft materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the mechanism of defect annealing and the transition from defect-rich polycrystalline to defect-free single-crystal states in active matter systems.
main_result: Defect annealing is shown to be controllable by tuning the spatiotemporal orientational fluctuations, suggesting that activity-assisted annealing can drive structural reorganization.
method: The research employs numerical simulations using overdamped Langevin equations of motion for Active Brownian Particles (ABPs) to model the coupled translational and rotational dynamics.
model_or_system: The system models active crystals, ranging from living organisms to artificial metamaterials, using ABPs interacting via a repulsive WCA potential. The dynamics are governed by Langevin equations incorporating active forces and torques.
key_observables: Crystallographic order (poly- to single-crystal), local hexatic order parameter ($g_6(r)$), global polar order parameter ($P$), and the number of remaining dislocations ($N_{	ext{dislo}}$).
important_parameters: Activity magnitude (Péclet number), persistence length ($	ext{l}_p$), and alignment timescales ($	au_p$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on separating the roles of activity magnitude, persistence, and alignment timescales, and sometimes assumes $	ext{l}_a \ll 	ext{l}_p$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of crystal order, the dependence of polar order on timescale control, and the sample-to-sample variability in defect annihilation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical problem (defect control), detailing the simulation setup and dynamics, and then systematically analyzing how tuning different activity timescales ($	au_p$ vs. $	ext{l}_p$) controls the annealing process and the resulting structural phase.
why_interesting: The concepts of non-equilibrium phase transitions, defect dynamics, and the role of active fluctuations in achieving ordered states are highly relevant to understanding open quantum systems and driven many-body dynamics.
